races.name: Hamilton Park Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up operator whose recent soft-going record reads just 3 qualifying runs with zero wins and zero places, making the ground a genuine concern despite the OK tag; Lexie Clarkson claims 7lb, but from OR 64 and a poor recent record over similar trips, needs things to go very right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler sends this 4-year-old out as the lone confirmed front-runner, but her promotional tag flags she is stepping into a lead role that her form — largely run from a prominent but not pace-making position — does not fully guarantee; just 2 qualifying runs on similar going with one win suggests soft conditions are not alien, and she gets in at 142lbs with Alex Jary aboard.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Smart soft-ground form figures prominently in her history (3rd on soft, 2nd on good to soft) and R Mike Smith has returned 2 from 21 runners in 14 days, showing quiet yard form; in reality a true hold-up horse, she is bumped into midfield on the map purely by the congestion at the rear, so her finishing kick may be blunted by a position forced too close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8 who routinely wears a hood (hg:p) to aid concentration and whose last five runs show only one placing (3rd), all on good ground — the soft surface here adds a layer of doubt; Linda Perratt's yard has had zero winners from ten runners in the past fortnight, and like others here he is sitting in midfield on the map despite being a natural rear-ranger.

runners_data.name: Realistic Dream
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by Iain Jardine, a trainer who has been placing 4 from 34 runners (12%) in the past 14 days, which is a notable positive; however, the horse's own record — 0W 0P from 4 runs on comparable going — and a form string of 965956 over distances including 7f and 6f suggest five furlongs on soft may be stretching her speed rather than her stamina.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Consistent runner with three consecutive runner-up finishes and strong going-comparable stats (5 runs, 0W 1P), suggesting soft or good-to-soft ground is not a problem; Jim Goldie has been busy and productive (7/30 in 14 days), and from a prominent pitch just behind the leader she is ideally placed to mount a sustained challenge in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls has 3 from just 6 runners in 14 days — a very strong strike rate — and this mare returns here having won over course and distance at 5f on good ground; her going-comparable record is the best in the field (10 qualifying runs, 1W 3P), and Jack Nicholls (trainer's son) ensures a confident tactical ride from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Consistent but quirky performer who wears a visor (hg:v) and is trained by the in-form Jim Goldie; his best recent form came over 6f on soft (1st) and 5f on good (3rd), but his soft-going qualifier count is just 1 from 15 runs, and being compressed into midfield from his natural rear-running role limits the chance of reproducing that winning effort at this shorter trip.

races.paceDynamic: Azuinthejungle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner sprint and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate from the gates at a sustainable but not scorching gallop on Good To Soft ground. Thunderstorm Katie and Thornaby Pearl will press prominently just off the pace, ensuring the front trio are grouped together early, but the absence of a true pace duel means Azuinthejungle is unlikely to be burned off. The hold-up contingent — Harb, Realistic Dream, Doon The Glen, Ski Angel and Sixcor — is unusually large for a 5-furlong field; several of these are true rear-runners who will find themselves racing against their instincts simply because there is no room at the front. This race shape, with a single uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo on soft-ish ground over five furlongs, strongly favours horses who can race prominently or make smooth headway from a close-up position, rather than those needing a true end-to-end gallop to drag them into contention. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than can realistically operate from the back — Doon The Glen, Ski Angel and Sixcor are all redistributed into midfield on the map, but Thornaby Pearl and Thunderstorm Katie are most likely to actually secure their natural prominent berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle sets an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent horses travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Azuinthejungle dictates from the front on her own terms, and horses like Thunderstorm Katie and Thornaby Pearl, sitting just off the pace, are ideally positioned to pounce in the final furlong without having used their reserves chasing a hot gallop. Good To Soft ground rewards those who have conserved energy through the race, and close-up runners who travel sweetly will have first run on anything held up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle finds the Good To Soft conditions to her liking and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap from their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the front end, Azuinthejungle could steal enough of a march to hold on as the closers — forced further back than ideal — fail to generate the finishing momentum needed over just five furlongs. This scenario is plausible precisely because so many of the hold-up types are racing out of their natural role and may lack the positioning to deliver a telling challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns out faster than expected and the front-runners tie each other up, leaving room for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Should Thunderstorm Katie push Azuinthejungle harder than anticipated, the pace could compromise both prominent runners, creating the one scenario where a horse getting back into its true hold-up role — most plausibly Ski Angel given her soft-ground form — could pick them up late. However, this scenario is discounted by the sheer number of redistributed hold-up types who are unlikely to get far back enough to produce a genuine finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the race shape is chaotic — crowding in the early stages or a slow early crawl followed by a sprint finish — and a lower-rated runner finds a dream run.
scenarios.body: A messy scenario where congestion in the large hold-up group leads to bumping or interference, creating a stop-start gallop that can produce a surprise result for a horse getting an uninterrupted passage. Doon The Glen, dropping back in trip and with recent soft-ground experience, is the most obvious beneficiary if the race disintegrates.

watchPoints.text: Thornaby Pearl — Adrian Nicholls is in sharp form (3/6 in 14 days) and this mare's course-and-distance form plus the strongest going-comparable record in the field makes her a genuine threat from a prominent position.

Azuinthejungle — as the sole front-runner she controls the tempo entirely, but her STYLE_FIT flag means she is not a natural leader; if she dwells or is taken back at the start the whole pace dynamic changes and there is no one to replace her at the head of affairs.

Hold-up cluster congestion — Harb, Doon The Glen, Ski Angel, Sixcor and Realistic Dream are all natural rear-runners competing for limited space behind the pace; watch for early crowding or interference that could further compromise already-disadvantaged horses.

Thunderstorm Katie's recent sequence of three consecutive second places suggests she is consistently hitting form but not winning — watch whether Rhys Elliott (3lb claimer) can produce a more positive ride to convert the placed form into a victory at a course where Jim Goldie's runners are firing.

Doon The Glen's visor and drop back to 5f from recent runs over 6f and beyond is worth monitoring in the early stages — if the headgear produces early speed he could position better than the map suggests, though soft-ground experience at this trip remains thin.

races.name: John & Margaret McCluskey Memorial Celebrations EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: Placed second on soft ground over 6f last time and carries the most useful form profile here; style unconfirmed but connections may look to slot in prominently given the pace vacuum, and 14 days since last run is a manageable absence for K.R. Burke.

runners_data.name: Hell Of A Spin
runners_data.note: Only run produced a second at 5f on Tapeta, so the surface switch to turf is the key unknown; Oisin McSweeney will need to dictate or at least press the pace to get the best out of this lightly-raced Keatley runner.

runners_data.name: River Jordan
runners_data.note: A 98-day absence is a concern for a two-year-old whose only start yielded a distant seventh on soft ground over 5f; Connor Beasley takes the ride but Phillip Makin's yard has had just one runner in 14 days and no wins, making this a watch-and-see proposition.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner has three consistent fourths and thirds to its name on good ground over 5f — solid form — but its natural inclination to race at the back of the field means it is drawn into midfield on this map only because every hold-up slot is filled; Mark Winn will need gaps to open up in the final furlong that a sprint finish may not provide.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Has shown some ability with a second from four starts and the form is respectable for this level, but the John & Sean Quinn runner is a genuine hold-up type that cannot get its preferred rear position here; Rhys Elliott on a 5lb claim adds appeal in theory, though the style mismatch tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides this Kevin Ryan-trained runner whose single outing saw a fourth on soft over 6f — arguably unlucky on trip rather than form — but its true hold-up style means it is shown in midfield on the map only through redistribution, and Stott may struggle to get it into a clean position in a field of similarly flat runners.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: The Fahey yard is in decent touch (6 wins from 64 in 14 days) but this runner's sole start produced a sixth on good over 6f, offering limited evidence for soft ground over 5f; Jack Garritty will need to find more than this form suggests unless conditions suit a hold-up type finding late momentum.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field, this 5f Hamilton maiden on Good to Soft is likely to begin with a scramble for early position rather than any single horse dictating a true pace. Casino Star, Hell Of A Spin, and My Mate Fitz are all unproven in terms of positional preference (style=U or H), meaning the early fractions will be dictated more by jockey intent than established pattern. The absence of a genuine pace-setter over a flat 5f suggests an honest but unspectacular tempo, with the field compressing into a sprint finish in the final two furlongs — a shape that typically rewards horses with a sharp, sustained burst rather than those needing a strong pace to close into. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Calef, Havana Gift, and My Mate Fitz are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the diagram, but in reality they cannot all secure the mid-division slot, and at least one will be forced wider or further back than ideal — the horses most likely to actually secure handy midfield berths are Calef and My Mate Fitz given their connections' tactical awareness. This race shape most favours a runner who can travel prominently without a confirmed lead to chase, pressing the pace through the bend and producing a clean, flat-ground finish — a prominent or close-tracking profile wins here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, No Leader
scenarios.trigger: If no horse asserts early and the field drifts at even tempo into a compressed sprint over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace-setter, the race becomes a question of who travels best through the early stages and has the punch to quicken on Good to Soft ground; horses who can be close to the pace without fighting for it hold the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Steals
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unproven or hold-up types is ridden more aggressively than usual and secures an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: A lone opportunist who finds the front by default from a field of non-confirmed leaders can dictate a comfortable rhythm on flat Hamilton terrain; Good to Soft ground rewards the horse who avoids the mid-pack scrimmage and gets a clean run throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the front runners tire in the final furlong on soft-ish ground.
scenarios.body: Genuinely soft conditions can stretch out a sprint and create a scenario where horses held up just off the pace finish strongly; however, this shape is undermined by the fact that Calef, Havana Gift, and My Mate Fitz — the true hold-up horses — are all racing out of their ideal position, reducing the reliability of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Firmer Surface Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the going is riding better than advertised and the track rewards natural early pace and a clean uncontested gallop.
scenarios.body: On a quicker-than-reported surface the premium shifts to horses with good enough form at this trip and the ability to sustain a sprint; Casino Star's second on soft over 6f and Hell Of A Spin's second at 5f are the most relevant profiles if conditions suit clean-running types.

watchPoints.text: Casino Star and Hell Of A Spin — if neither establishes early, watch for a chaotic first two furlongs where no horse gets a clean lead and the tempo becomes ragged, distorting the race entirely.

Calef, Havana Gift, and My Mate Fitz — all three are true hold-up horses mapped into midfield; if they bunch together in the early stages, watch for traffic problems and blocked runs through the final furlong.

River Jordan — a 98-day layoff for a two-year-old on soft ground is a significant flag; watch for signs of ring-rustiness early, which could further disrupt any rhythm if it checks or weakens in the pack.

Going report confirms Good to Soft for this race, not the Soft declared in the race heading — a materially faster surface that will compress the finishing spread and reduce the advantage of any hold-up horse relying on rivals to tie themselves up.

races.name: Rocca Restaurant & Ora Bar Hamilton Handicap

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here with three recent 6f placings including a win and a second on soft ground; Jack Garritty knows this horse well, and an uncontested lead over this trip and going is exactly the scenario his profile demands — STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant here as he is the natural pace-setter in this field.

runners_data.name: Not Me
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has done his best recent work over 6f-8f on soft, landing a win at 8f/Soft last time; Alan Brown's yard is out of form (0/8 in 14 days) and the return to 6f from longer trips is a slight query, but soft-ground form is a genuine asset.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Strong soft-ground form with a win at 6f/Soft and two other placings at the trip — this is her optimum conditions; a natural hold-up horse nudged into the map's midfield due to field composition, and the blinkered headgear plus Connor Beasley are positives, though an 8yo needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 6f last time and has multiple 6f placings, but soft-going form is limited (11th in his only 5f/Soft start); visor retained, and David O'Meara's yard is in solid form (6/47 in 14 days), yet as a true hold-up type mapped forward, his chance depends on the race not being run to suit a wire-to-wire winner.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: 358 days off the track is a serious concern — last soft-ground run produced a 19th place finish and she has not shown form on this going; Richard & Peter Fahey are active (4/50), but a first run back after almost a year for a horse whose recent record is uninspiring makes her a significant risk at any price.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with all his best work over 7f, making 6f a slightly sharp query; recent form is solid (1st and 3rd in last four at 7f) and Jim Goldie's yard is in form (6/46), but a 5-day turnaround and the step down in trip mean he needs a truly run race to show his best — as a redistributed hold-up type he may struggle to land a blow from deep.

races.paceDynamic: Ingleby Archie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no identified challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested, controlled position from the outset on Good to Soft ground over 6f at Hamilton. The pace will be genuine but sustainable — a single leader dictating from flag to flag without being pressured creates a steady, rhythmic gallop that suits those who can track close to the action rather than those coming from deep. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up types — Not Me, Eartha, Iris Dancer, Come On Over, and Ashen all want to be covered up — meaning the race shape is heavily weighted toward a front-runner's benefit rather than those hunting the leader from the rear. Three of those hold-up runners (Iris Dancer, Come On Over, Ashen) are redistributed in the map because the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the rear positions can accommodate, with Ingleby Archie and — to a lesser degree — any horse willing to push forward from the Prominent slot most likely to actually secure their natural position. This race shape strongly favours a pressing, prominent-to-lead profile: an unchallenged leader on soft ground over a flat 6f Hamilton is a powerful tactical advantage, and those who track closely in second or third will be best placed to pounce if the leader tires late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ingleby Archie Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie bowls clear from the gates and encounters no pace pressure throughout the 6f.
scenarios.body: Ingleby Archie sets a controlled, solo tempo on Good to Soft ground, conserving enough energy to sustain his gallop to the line; the hold-up field is left with too much ground to make up from off the pace on a flat track where momentum is everything.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Soft ground rides softer than the going report suggests, slowing the early pace enough to compress the field.
scenarios.body: Ingleby Archie's lead narrows significantly in the final furlong as the ground saps his stamina, and the freshest hold-up runners finish fastest; genuine soft-ground form becomes the key differentiator.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up runner breaks more prominently than expected and tracks Ingleby Archie closely enough to challenge from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The compressed, small field allows a horse who travels into a handy second or third to attack the leader approaching the final furlong before he can fully assert; this scenario rewards horses with tactical versatility on today's trip and going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie goes too fast for the conditions and weakens sharply inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The whole field converges in a dramatic late finish as the leader fades, rewarding those who had the most energy conserved and the sharpest turn of foot; soft-ground specialists and lightly-weighted hold-up types are best placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Ingleby Archie gets away cleanly and is bowled along without a single rival willing to go with him — watch whether any horse breaks prominently at the start, as a totally uncontested lead dramatically increases his winning chance.

Eartha is 358 days off the track and has a poor record on soft ground — monitor her in the paddock and at the start for any signs of ring-rustiness, as she could be a non-runner or a dangerous obstacle for horses behind her if she is reluctant to settle.

Iris Dancer, Come On Over, and Ashen are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into the mid-section of the map — if all three try to chase from behind on a flat 6f track with one leader, the closers may simply not generate enough pace to catch Ingleby Archie, making their collective finishing power less potent than it looks on paper.

The going report lists this race as Good to Soft despite the GOING field showing Soft — monitor any official downgrade closer to race time, as softer ground would lengthen the race significantly for the hold-up brigade and place more premium on genuine soft-ground form, where Iris Dancer and Not Me hold an advantage over Come On Over.

races.name: racingtv.com Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has a consistent hold-up profile with recent form showing a run of mid-pack finishes over shorter distances on Good ground — stepping up to 1m5f and Good To Soft may help, but five consecutive out-of-frame finishes on Good over 10-12f offer limited encouragement that the form is travelling forward at present.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jura
runners_data.note: The key pace-maker in this race and the only confirmed front-runner; Connor Beasley will likely take them straight to the front unchallenged, but similar-going figures of 0 wins and 0 places from 2 runs on soft-equivalent ground is a meaningful flag, and the horse's OR of 81 leaves little room for error if the gallop is steady enough to let the stalkers travel.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott (5lb claimer) takes over on a horse whose record on soft-equivalent going reads encouragingly — two wins and two places from five qualifying runs — and a win over 10f on Good last time out suggests this 1m5f trip should be well within range; true hold-up style means the horse needs some cut in the pace to make the late effort count.|

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old carries the lightest weight in the field at 125lbs and has a genuinely prominent, race-riding profile that suits the expected shape perfectly — a win over 12f on Good last time out and four placed efforts from 15 runs on soft-equivalent ground confirms both the trip and conditions are compatible; Jack Nicholls (5lb claimer) keeps the weight advantage live.|

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans's charge is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the field's composition means racing from the rear is unlikely to be available — Kevin Stott will need to adapt and ride more positively than the horse's usual pattern, which the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 flags as a meaningful dilution of its chance; placed three times from four similar-going runs, the ability in conditions is not in doubt.|

runners_data.name: Ameilya
runners_data.note: Stuart Coltherd sends out a mare whose recent form figures of 70/6-8 include two runs over today's 1m5f+ range on soft going with no notable success — a natural hold-up runner whose true position is the rear but who, in this six-runner field, will be pushed closer than ideal; the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/4 adds to the background concerns.|

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Jura is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field over 1m5f on Good To Soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, they will likely bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo that could prove deceptively steady through the early stages. Dunkeld Dreamer is the other prominent-style runner and will track Spirit Of Jura, creating a small lead group but not enough competition to force a genuine test of stamina from the front. The trio of Prince Of The Seas, Spirit Of Acklam, Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya all carry hold-up profiles to varying degrees, though Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya are genuine rear-runners who have been mapped to midfield because the field cannot accommodate all of them at the back — the true rear positions are likely to belong to Prince Of The Seas and Spirit Of Acklam, with Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya potentially forced to race closer than ideal. With a single uncontested pace-setter setting a sustainable gallop on a flat track, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track the leader in a stalking position and produce a controlled late effort — making Dunkeld Dreamer's prominent, race-riding profile the most naturally suited in this shape, while true hold-up runners face the risk of a pace that does not truly soften up the leaders sufficiently for a late burst to prove decisive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Jura dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and Dunkeld Dreamer tracks in second throughout before producing a sustained run from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Jura sets a comfortable rhythm that never truly stress-tests the field for stamina, allowing the prominent stalker to exploit a clean passage and outstay rivals who are held up too far back to land a telling blow; the flat Hamilton track means there is no bend or gradient to disrupt a well-positioned hold-up runner, but a steady pace blunts the finishers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely unhurried and Spirit Of Jura steals enough of an advantage through the final turn that pursuers cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: On Good To Soft ground over this flat 1m5f circuit, a horse allowed to bowl along without pressure can conserve energy and find stamina reserves that overcome a modest rating; Connor Beasley is an experienced handler of front-running situations and could judge the fractions perfectly to deny the chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently from 3f out to string out the field and create a gap for a horse delivered late with a single run.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires Spirit Of Acklam or Prince Of The Seas to find clear daylight in a small six-runner field and produce a finishing effort that overcomes the steady early fractions — possible but reliant on the pace being faster than the race shape suggests; Spirit Of Acklam's two wins from 12 similar-going runs and course-appropriate profile give the most realistic claim here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If there is jostling for position early, the pace becomes uneven and the race degenerates into a stop-start affair that scrambles the expected order.
scenarios.body: An uneven tempo over 1m5f on soft ground can produce a chaotic finish where horses who were outpaced briefly are able to recover and close — Sure And Stedfast, whose natural hold-up style is compressed into midfield, could find this messy shape accidentally suits; however, the small field and flat track make a genuinely chaotic scenario unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Of Jura's uncontested lead is the hinge of the entire race — watch whether Connor Beasley uses the advantage to construct a slow-burn, stamina-sapping gallop or simply idles in front, as the tempo chosen in the first half-mile will define whether Dunkeld Dreamer stalks within range or floats into a false position.

Sure And Stedfast and Ameilya are both natural rear-runners who cannot realistically both get the back-of-the-field berth they prefer — watch the early stages for one or both being forced to race at least two lengths closer than their form has been built around, which could compromise their finishing efforts significantly.

Dunkeld Dreamer's jockey Jack Nicholls (apprentice, 5lb) is relatively inexperienced in a race where controlling the stalking position behind Spirit Of Jura is the key tactical job — watch whether he can maintain a clean, uninterrupted line through the early stages without being crowded by the repositioning hold-up horses.

Spirit Of Acklam is 28 days since last running and steps into a soft-ground contest where their record is notably strong — watch for signs in the paddock and early race that the horse is travelling well within itself, as a fresh hold-up type who handles these conditions is the most credible late threat to the prominent pair.

races.name: Get Your Tickets For Cube Glass Ladies Night Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing four-year-old for David O'Meara and Mark Winn, only 12 days since last run, handles good ground well but has a single placing at 9f on similar going from two relevant runs — the step up to 1m½f on soft needs to click but the race shape suits.|

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's hold-up type has a genuine soft-ground win on the board (1/8f/SOF) making him the most credible closer in the field; Dougie Costello rides, and 21 days since last run is fine, though the anticipated controlled pace limits how much ground he can realistically make up.|

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's five-year-old won at 8f on Good and placed on Soft, but this horse's instinct is to race prominently — the crowded front end means it is likely to find itself shuffled back into a midfield position that does not play to its natural strengths, tempering confidence in its chance.|

runners_data.name: Lucky Camino
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner; Kevin Stott can control the tempo unchallenged over 1m½f, and three consecutive placed efforts including a soft-ground second suggest the horse handles the ground and will be tough to dislodge if allowed to dictate.|

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old carries the lowest weight (129lbs) and won over 8f on Good, but like Quiet Resolve its forward-going tendencies are compromised here — there simply is not room for it at the head of affairs, and racing from a deeper position than preferred is a notable negative in this map.|

runners_data.name: Showcasing Star
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on Charlie Johnston's three-year-old who has placed four times from five runs on Turf but is yet to win; the hold-up style over this trip needs a stronger pace than Lucky Camino is likely to set, and the soft-ground form line (7/8f/SOF) is modest.|

races.paceDynamic: Lucky Camino is the one confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners over 1m½f on Good to Soft ground at Hamilton, Kevin Stott should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset without being pressed. Kaleido is the only genuine prominent type likely to sit close to Lucky Camino's quarters, while Zowal and Showcasing Star will settle in the rear half and look to close late. Quiet Resolve and Sanafi Zabeel are both natural prominent horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more pace-seeking types in this field than can realistically secure those forward positions — Lucky Camino and Kaleido are most likely to monopolise the front rank, leaving Quiet Resolve and Sanafi Zabeel racing out of their preferred role. A controlled pace set by a single, uncontested front-runner over a stamina-testing trip on soft ground strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to sit handy and quicken from a prominent position, rather than those forced to close from further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lucky Camino Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Camino dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the field settles behind without challenging for the lead.
scenarios.body: Kevin Stott sends Lucky Camino to the front and the soft ground rewards a horse that relaxes and travels smoothly, building a lead that proves hard to reel in over this stamina test. Prominent and close-tracking horses benefit most, with the run-in at Hamilton offering insufficient distance for deep hold-up types to deliver a telling late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kaleiko Picks Up The Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Camino sets a tempo that drains its own reserves in the soft ground and Kaleido, sitting just off the pace, reels it in late.
scenarios.body: Kaleido tracks Lucky Camino throughout from a prominent berth, conserving enough energy to collar the front-runner inside the final furlong as the testing surface takes its toll on the pacesetter. The four-year-old's proximity to the action means it avoids the late-closer disadvantage and its one placing over similar going last time out supports the ground claim.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true test of stamina, enabling the deep closers to finish through.
scenarios.body: Zowal and Showcasing Star, racing from the rear, would need both a strong early gallop and a clear run to make up meaningful ground over this trip; Zowal's win on soft ground is the key credentials, though the anticipated controlled pace makes this scenario less probable. Showcasing Star has shown consistent placed form at this level but has yet to win, making a late swoop plausible only if conditions conspire against the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Grab Prominent Spot
scenarios.trigger: If the pre-race order breaks down at the start and Quiet Resolve or Sanafi Zabeel are able to force their way into a genuinely prominent position rather than sitting in midfield.
scenarios.body: Both horses are natural pace-seekers mapped to midfield due to the crowded front end, and if circumstances allow one to push forward, it races more in role and could outperform its map position. This is a low-probability shape because Lucky Camino and Kaleido are expected to dominate the front rank and leave no natural gap for these two to slot into.

watchPoints.text: Lucky Camino (Kevin Stott) is the only horse certain to lead — watch whether it is allowed to bowl along entirely unchallenged, as an uncontested front-runner on soft ground over this trip has a significant advantage in this six-runner field.

Quiet Resolve and Sanafi Zabeel are both natural front-seekers who cannot both get their preferred position — watch the early stages to see which, if either, pushes forward and which is forced to drop back, as that will reshape who is racing in role.
Zowal's hold-up style is dependent on the pace being strong enough; if Lucky Camino dawdles, watch whether Dougie Costello opts to alter tactics and move him closer earlier than planned.

Showcasing Star has a string of seconds on Standard ground but only one run on Soft — watch how Connor Beasley positions it early, as an inability to travel smoothly in the conditions would end its chance before the straight.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who gets a dream solo lead here; soft-ground record is modest (one win from 15 similar-going runs) but uncontested control on a flat 1m½f circuit plays to its strengths, though racing at OR=61 on a seven-year-old frame with 141lbs is a stamina question late.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Won over this trip on good ground last time and showed finishing speed; Kevin Stott takes over and this five-year-old has the profile of a horse who can sit just off the pace and stay — soft-ground form is limited at one win from 15, but the recent course-and-distance win is the standout angle.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's nine-year-old genuinely wants to come from off the pace — a true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map position because there are simply too many closers in this field; soft ground suits (3 from 15) but age and a run of consecutive fifths make it hard to back with confidence.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: The three-year-old carries headgear (p) and has placed twice on soft ground from six tries, sitting as the natural prominent runner behind Second Fiddle; Dougie Costello is a key booking and stepping up to 1m½f from 8f looks like a trainer aiming at the trip rather than against it.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Perratt's four-year-old carries headgear (p) and has been beaten in double figures across recent soft and good-to-soft outings at shorter trips — the step to 1m½f is significant, and its natural inclination to come from behind is compromised by a field stacked with other hold-up horses; Finlay Bassett's 7lb claim helps the weight but the form string reads uninspiringly.

runners_data.name: Amber Hamur
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old ran just 8 days ago and placed second on good ground over 8f — the step up in trip could unlock improvement, and Connor Beasley is a quality booking; a genuine hold-up runner whose late finish will depend on whether Second Fiddle's tempo is strong enough to create a true test.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has finished outside the first four in all five recent starts including two nines, and the form string offers little encouragement; Mark Winn takes the ride but this is another deep hold-up type stacked behind rivals with better recent profiles, and soft ground has not been visited often enough to gauge confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Second Fiddle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m½f handicap on good-to-soft ground at Hamilton, and with no genuine challenger likely to press for the lead, Jack Nicholls can dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the front. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Hostelry, Defence Missile, Ten Sixty Six, and Amber Hamur all want to come from off the pace — meaning the pace is unlikely to be hot enough to set up a dramatic late swoop. Positive Thoughts is the one prominent-style runner who may push up to sit just behind Second Fiddle, giving the leader at least one shadow, but not the sustained pressure that would drain stamina. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can quickest respond to Second Fiddle's tempo change, yet because the pace is controlled and the ground soft, those who can sit closest to the modest early gallop and produce a sustained finish — rather than a pure late burst — are most advantaged; the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the track map can accommodate at the rear, with Second Fiddle and Positive Thoughts most certain to secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle is allowed to bowl along uncontested and the steady pace on soft ground suits a one-paced gallop that grinds out the closers.
scenarios.body: Second Fiddle dictates every yard from the front under Nicholls, the soft ground blunting the finish of the hold-up horses as they cannot generate enough pace from off a modest tempo to collar the leader; this is the textbook scenario for a lone front-runner on a sound-surface track where no rival wants to take them on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts or Daring Leader sit tight just off the pace and deliver a sustained challenge from two furlongs out that gradually wears down Second Fiddle.
scenarios.body: The leader's stamina is tested as the most economically-ridden stalker cruises into contention from the two-pole and edges ahead in the closing stages on the softened ground; this suits a horse with strong soft-ground form that has been asked to settle just off the lead rather than chase a late winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally quicker than expected, stringing the field out and leaving enough gaps for a strong finisher to thread through late.
scenarios.body: One of the displaced hold-up types — most likely Amber Hamur or Daring Leader — manages to find a path through tired rivals from the two-furlong pole and benefits from the soft ground rewarding pure stamina over raw speed; this is the scenario that demands a genuinely searching gallop, which is not guaranteed given Second Fiddle's likely comfort on the front end.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle is pressured unexpectedly or the gallop is so slow that it turns into a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A bunched field fans wide in the straight and a horse with a sharp turn of foot rather than pure stamina capitalises; this heavily discounted scenario requires redistribution of several horses into unnatural roles and depends on tactics that are unlikely given the clear front-runner dominance and soft ground.

watchPoints.text: Second Fiddle (Nicholls) sets the entire race tempo — if it is allowed to bowl along undisturbed at the top of the home straight, the race is over as a contest for pace; watch whether any rival challenges for the lead in the first half-mile.

Positive Thoughts (Costello) with the hood on is the one horse likely to track Second Fiddle directly — if it moves to the leader's girths turning into the straight, it becomes the primary danger and the race shape shifts to Scenario B immediately.

Amber Hamur (Beasley) ran only 8 days ago and will be ridden to come late; watch its position at the two-furlong pole — if it is still more than three lengths off the pace on this soft ground, it may not find enough to close.

The entire hold-up quartet (Hostelry, Defence Missile, Ten Sixty Six, Amber Hamur) cannot all be accommodated at the rear without severely compromising their runs — watch the early jostling for position between two furlongs after the start to see who gets shuffled widest.

Soft ground is confirmed but previous results at Hamilton over 1m½f on similar going (7:50 race same card) are worth checking post-race for any rail or draw bias that may further assist the lone leader tracking the stands-side rail.

races.name: Follow Us On X At HamiltonParkRC Handicap

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old handicapper with a legitimate soft-going profile (1W2P from 15 similar-ground starts) but a modest recent string of 48-006 raises stamina-fitness questions over 1m3f; Jim Goldie's yard is running at 6/36 (17%) over 14 days and the hood is retained, suggesting connections are persisting with a plan — true hold-up style suits a genuine test.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott takes the ride on this five-year-old who has shown ability on good-to-soft (2nd at Southwell, 3rd at Hamilton) but has managed only 0W1P from 15 similar-going runs; her natural hold-up style means she could be squeezed for room early with so many back-markers in this field, and a style-fit score of 0.93 flags genuine concern about getting a clean run in this congested shape.

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a light but encouraging CV — won over 8f at Southwell (standard) and placed twice on soft, and now steps up to 1m3f with Jack Nicholls (5) in the saddle; the headgear notation (hood) is noted, and his soft-ground certificate is legitimate, though this is a first attempt at the trip which introduces a clear question mark.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old arrives 32 days between runs with a record that shows placed form on soft (2nd over 8f) but nothing beyond 9f yet — his hold-up instincts are real, yet this field's configuration means he could find himself racing more prominently than suits him, and his style-fit of 0.90 is a tangible discount on his chances if the race doesn't run to a true hold-up shape.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: The only runner without a confirmed style tag, trained by Edward Bethell (2/30 in 14 days) and ridden by Cian Horgan (5); four career runs show modest form (best finish 4th) and no wins or places on soft, but his unknown style is actually the tactical wild card — if he drifts forward by default, he could set the terms of this race without intending to.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has the most compelling profile in this field for a muddled-pace scenario — a winner over 9f on soft and placed over 12f at Southwell, with Connor Beasley booked and only 19 days between runs; despite being a natural off-the-pace runner, he is the most likely of the three redistributed hold-up horses to edge forward given his recent winning confidence and Beasley's positional awareness.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field, this 1m3f Hamilton contest on Good To Soft ground is set to unfold at a muddled, moderate tempo with no horse likely to take a commanding lead from the off. Clocker (style unknown) is the lone runner without a confirmed hold-up profile, leaving a vacuum at the head of affairs that could produce a dawdling gallop until riders are forced to commit on the final bend. The absence of a genuine pace-maker on soft ground over this trip is critical — a slow-run race that collapses into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs will compress the field and reduce the premium on stamina. Jujubella, Mr Moonshine, and Port Darwin are all true hold-up types redistibuted to the map's midfield because this field contains more off-the-pace runners than there are rear positions to fill — of those three, Port Darwin (Connor Beasley, won over 9f soft) is best-placed to naturally assert a forward position given his recent winning form, while Jujubella and Mr Moonshine are most vulnerable to racing further up than ideal. This race shape squarely favours horses with tactical versatility or an explosive short-range finish, as the slow pace on soft ground will reward those who can quicken off a compressed gallop rather than those who need a true test of stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles early and the race only ignites inside the final 2f, creating a bunched finish off a slow gallop.
scenarios.body: No horse imposes early tempo, riders drift into a tentative rhythm, and the race is decided by a short, sharp burst rounding the home bend; runners with the best finishing kick over soft ground will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Port Darwin Dictates Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Port Darwin or Clocker nudges forward to set a genuine but measured pace and controls the race from the front.
scenarios.body: A steady, honest gallop develops with Port Darwin's recent soft-ground winning form giving him the fitness edge to dictate terms and hold on; horses tracking the loose leader from second or third are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely true-run pace develops and the field is strung out, leaving room for hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: Spanish Hustle (sim-going record of 5 runs on soft, handicap experience) and Ibn Altheeb can come from off the pace if there is something to chase down; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact that most hold-up runners here are true back-markers squeezed into midfield, reducing the chance of a textbook late rally.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Field
scenarios.trigger: If rain intensifies the going further and a searching stamina test separates the field decisively in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Genuine soft-ground handlers with proven staying ability over 10f+ will pull clear of those found wanting by the conditions; Spanish Hustle's soft-ground profile (1W2P in 15 similar-going runs) and Ibn Altheeb's soft certificate offer the clearest claims.

watchPoints.text: Watch Clocker's early behaviour — as the only runner without a confirmed style, if Cian Horgan (5) allows him to drift to the front by default, he becomes an accidental pace-setter who could set the terms for the entire race on soft ground.

Port Darwin, Jujubella, and Mr Moonshine are all natural hold-up types crammed into a small field where rear positions will be congested; monitor the early stages for interference or horses being switched wider than ideal, which could cost lengths on a soft surface.

Ibn Altheeb steps up in trip for the first time to 1m3f — watch whether Jack Nicholls (5) attempts to use him positively early to avoid the hold-up traffic, as any sign of inexperience at the new distance on soft ground could be telling.

Spanish Hustle is the eldest horse in the field at eight years old and carries 142lbs — watch his action going to post on the soft ground for any sign of labour, as top weight on this surface could blunt his finishing effort if the race does develop into a genuine stamina test.
